findings.title: CVE-2026-107412 (NetScaler CNA JSON 5.1 Record)
findings.summary_md: The NetScaler CNA reserved CVE-2026-107412 on 2026-10-08 at 00:18:26 UTC in the CVE JSON 5.1 record, with datePublic set to 2026-11-12T23:05:00Z and datePublished set to 2026-11-13T02:21:30Z. The record covers multiple memory overflow vulnerabilities (CWE-119) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway versions prior to 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS, and 13.1-37.293 FIPs and NDcPP when configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or an AAA virtual server. It assigns CVSS v4.0 base score 9.5 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H) and references Citrix bulletin CTX697305.

findings.title: Angreifer koennen Citrix NetScaler ADC und NetScaler Gateway lahmlegen (heise online)
findings.summary_md: heise online published Dennis Schirrmacher's initial German-language report at 15:24 CET (14:24:00Z) on 2026-11-12 covering Citrix bulletin CTX697305, which patches 28 memory flaws across NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway (9 rated critical and 15 rated high). The article notes that CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 9.3) affects default packet-processing configurations on all appliances, while CVE-2026-107412 (CVSS 9.5) is rated the most severe and requires the appliance to be configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or an AAA virtual server. It records that Citrix has received no reports of active exploitation, that Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments using customer-managed NetScaler instances are affected, and that remediating builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS, and 13.1-37.293.

findings.title: Netscaler Apocalypse? Security Bulletin CTX697305 (Borns IT- und Windows-Blog)
findings.summary_md: Günter Born reported on 2026-11-12 at 18:29:58Z that Citrix published security bulletin CTX697305 for NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, fixing 28 vulnerabilities in supported branches prior to 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS, and 13.1-37.293. The post also notes that Cloud Software Group introduced a new Security Release Program announced on Monday 2026-11-09 to give customer maintenance teams advance visibility before monthly CVE publications, and that Cloud Software Group used AI-assisted code analysis alongside external researchers from watchTowr and JPMorgan Chase to identify flaws in the batch. Same-day companion bulletins CTX697280, CTX697281, and CTX697320 addressed Secure Access Client for Windows, Secure Access Client for Linux, and NetScaler Console.

findings.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway Security Bulletin (CTX697305)
findings.summary_md: Citrix support article CTX697305 (schema.org publication timestamp 2026-11-12 20:27 UTC) documents 28 vulnerabilities across NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway, including CVE-2026-107412 at CVSS v4.0 9.5 (CWE-119). Preconditions for CVE-2026-107412 require the appliance to be configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or an AAA virtual server, testable by searching the running configuration for `add vpn vserver` or `add authentication vserver`. Fixed versions are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS, and 13.1-37.293, with credits listing Michael Tucker and Chew Keong Tan of the XOR team at JPMorgan Chase, Kyle Hannon of CapitalOne Offensive Security, Himanshu Anand and Sina Kheirkhah of watchTowr, and the Cloud Software Group Product Security Team.

findings.title: Citrix NetScaler: 28 Lücken im Bulletin CTX697305 (S-EDV)
findings.summary_md: S-EDV published an analysis of Citrix bulletin CTX697305 at 02:21:46 CET (01:21:46Z) on 2026-11-13, detailing the 28 NetScaler ADC and Gateway vulnerabilities, 9 of which carry a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3 or higher. It highlights that CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 9.3) affects every default NetScaler installation, while CVE-2026-107412 (CVSS 9.5) targets Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) and AAA virtual servers, and notes that multiple CVSS 4.0 vectors rate confidentiality and integrity as HIGH despite Citrix framing the impact as denial of service. It recommends inventorying all NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances including Secure Private Access nodes, upgrading internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances first to 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS, or 13.1-37.293, keeping NSIP management addresses off the public internet, and monitoring for post-update crashes and restarts.
